after.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩, \\ N(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{cos}⁡3t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
after.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩\times ⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,0,-\operatorname{cos}⁡3t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0 \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =⟨0-0,-(-{cos}^{2}⁡3t-{sin}^{2}⁡3t),0-0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2{e}^{t},{e}^{t},1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
after.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2{e}^{t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}},\,\frac{{e}^{t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}},\,-\frac{5{e}^{2t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}⟨2{e}^{t},\,{e}^{t},\,-5{e}^{2t}⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{(2{e}^{t})^{2}+{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-5{e}^{2t})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{4{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+25{e}^{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}{e}^{t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{1+5{e}^{2t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}{e}^{t}}{5{e}^{2t}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}⟨2{e}^{t},\,{e}^{t},\,-5{e}^{2t}⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{5}{e}^{t}}{5{e}^{2t}+1})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2,\,1,\,-5{e}^{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2{e}^{t},{e}^{t},1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2,\,1,\,-5{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & 1 \\ 1 & -5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} & 1 \\ 2 & -5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}⟨-5{e}^{2t}-1,-(-10{e}^{2t}-2),2{e}^{t}-2{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}⟨-(5{e}^{2t}+1),\,2(5{e}^{2t}+1),\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2{e}^{t},{e}^{t},1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
content.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2{e}^{t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}},\,\frac{{e}^{t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}},\,-\frac{5{e}^{2t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}⟨2{e}^{t},\,{e}^{t},\,-5{e}^{2t}⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{(2{e}^{t})^{2}+{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-5{e}^{2t})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{4{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+25{e}^{4t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}{e}^{t}}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}\sqrt{1+5{e}^{2t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}{e}^{t}}{5{e}^{2t}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{(5{e}^{2t}+1)^{3/2}}⟨2{e}^{t},\,{e}^{t},\,-5{e}^{2t}⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{5}{e}^{t}}{5{e}^{2t}+1})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2,\,1,\,-5{e}^{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2{e}^{t},{e}^{t},1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨2,\,1,\,-5{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & 1 \\ 1 & -5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} & 1 \\ 2 & -5{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}⟨-5{e}^{2t}-1,-(-10{e}^{2t}-2),2{e}^{t}-2{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(5{e}^{2t}+1)}⟨-(5{e}^{2t}+1),\,2(5{e}^{2t}+1),\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-1,2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
after.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}})}=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨0-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-(0-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\sqrt{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t+\sqrt{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
content.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}})}=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨0-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-(0-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\sqrt{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t+\sqrt{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

after.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(0) & =T(0)\times N(0) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨(0-0),-(-1-1),(0-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,2,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}

content.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=0$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,1⟩, \\ N(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
content.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(0) & =T(0)\times N(0) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨(0-0),-(-1-1),(0-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,2,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
